digest.component_or_area: store usability detection and read/write parity
propositions: _reads._tracker fires store_uninitialized only when tracker directory is absent, not when it exists but is unusable (no .git, unresolvable HEAD, marker files only), causing broken stores to return [] indistinguishably from empty initialized stores

A present-but-unusable store (marker files, no .git, or .git with unresolvable HEAD) must raise store_uninitialized instead of [] to restore read/write parity with event_prepare._ensure_initialized, which already guards on .git presence

Materialized snapshots checked out as .git-less directories with committed .store-compat.json and event data must remain readable despite lacking .git, requiring the usability predicate to detect store structure alongside git/HEAD presence

A unified store_is_usable predicate used by both _reads._tracker and _ensure_initialized prevents read/write divergence, with clauses for (.git + resolvable HEAD) OR (.store-compat.json present) OR (≥1 non-dot event dir)

The HEAD-resolution probe must use bounded git execution (gitutil.run_git_bounded with timeout) to preserve the write-path invariant that no lock-held git call runs unbounded, avoiding indefinite hold on the store write lock
Empty materialized snapshots (.git-less, .store-compat.json, zero events) are valid and must read [] rather than raise, confirming the predicate is never keyed on emptiness
